title: Controlling Electrospun Polymer Morphology for Tissue Engineering Demonstrated Using hepG2 Cell Line
protocol: Prepare a 5:1 ratio of chloroform and methanol by mixing 50 mL of chloroform and 10 mL of methanol in a glass solvent-proof bottle using a glass serological pipette.
Weigh 1.9 g of PCL and add to 10 mL of 5:1 chloroform:methanol in a glass solvent-proof vial.
Double seal the vial using paraffin film and leave on a roller overnight to allow the PCL to fully dissolve.
Weigh 0.7 g of PCL and mix with 10 mL of HFIP in a glass solvent-proof vial.
Double seal the vial using paraffin film and leave on a roller overnight to allow the PCL to fully dissolve.
Mix 30 mL of chloroform and 10 mL of methanol in a glass solvent-proof bottle using a glass serological pipette.
Weigh 1.4 g of PCL and add it to 10 mL of 3:1 chloroform:methanol in a glass solvent-proof vial.
Double seal the vial using paraffin film.
Leave the vial on a roller overnight to allow PCL to fully dissolve.
Use a 1 mm OD/0.8 mm ID brass needle for large fibers, placing it 230 mm away from the mandrel surface.
Use a 1 mm OD/0.4 mm ID brass needle for small fibers, placing it 15 mm away from the mandrel surface.
Set Start position [mm] to -50, Distance [mm] to 100, Speed [mm/s] to 50 and Turn Delay [ms] to 750 for lateral needle motion.
Set syringe pump flow rate to 4 mL/h for large fibers by pressing the Material tab on the user interface.
Set syringe pump flow rate to 0.8 mL/h for small fibers by pressing the Material tab on the user interface.
Set syringe pump flow rate to 2.5 mL/h for small cryogenic fibers by pressing the Material tab on the user interface.
Set needle voltage at +15 kV and mandrel voltage at -4 kV for large fibers by pressing the Voltage tab on the user interface.
Set the needle voltage at +17 kV for small random and aligned fibers.
Set the needle voltage at +18 kV for small cryogenic fibers.
Set the mandrel voltage at -4 kV for both small random, aligned, and cryogenic fibers.
Press Motion | Target to set the mandrel rotation speed to 250 rpm for random fibers.
Set the mandrel rotation speed to 1,800 rpm for aligned fibers.
Set the mandrel rotation speed to 180 rpm for cryogenic fibers.
Insert the needle into 1 mm bore PTFE tubing and secure it within the electrospinner needle holder.
Transfer 10 mL of polymer solution into a polypropylene or glass syringe under a fume hood.
Remove any bubbles from the syringe by letting it stand before priming.
Connect the syringe to the needle via the PTFE tubing and secure the syringe within the syringe pump.
Prime the PTFE tubing by squeezing the syringe plunger and filling the tube with polymer solution.
Wrap the mandrel in aluminum foil and secure it onto the mandrel rotation device.
Switch on the mandrel rotation by pressing Motion | Target | Rotate.
Start the syringe pump by pressing Material | Start Pump 1.
Switch on the voltage by pressing ACTIVATE HIGH VOLTAGE after forming a bead of polymer at the needle end.
Check the mandrel for fiber deposition during electrospinning.
Remove the aluminum foil covered with fibers from the mandrel after termination of the process and leave it in a fume cupboard overnight to evaporate excess solvent.
Store the dried fibers at room temperature (RT).
Wrap the cryo-spinning mandrel in aluminum foil.
Fill the mandrel with dry ice pellets for cryogenic electrospinning.
Secure the cover onto the mandrel to allow pressure escape but prevent dry ice loss.
Place the mandrel on the rotation device and start both mandrel rotation and syringe pump.
Switch on the voltage by pressing ACTIVATE HIGH VOLTAGE once a bead of polymer has formed at the end of the needle.
Check the mandrel to confirm fiber deposition on the mandrel surface after switching on the voltage.
Pause the electrospinning process by pressing STOP ALL after 1 hour of operation.
Top up the mandrel with dry ice and refill it, ensuring adequate protection from solvent vapor.
Repeat steps 4.4 and 4.5 for a total of 3 times to achieve 4 hours of electrospinning time.
Remove the mandrel carefully once electrospinning ends and place it into a freeze drier for 24 hours to sublimate ice crystals on the mandrel surface.
Carefully remove fiber-covered foil from the mandrel after sublimation and store at room temperature, avoiding crushing.
Punch scaffolds from the sheet of fibers using a 10-12 mm biopsy punch.
Place scaffolds in 70% ethanol to facilitate detachment if they remain adhered to the aluminum foil.
Sterilize scaffolds by washing them 3 times with 70% ethanol.
Submerge scaffolds in the final wash and place into a -80°C freezer until frozen.
Lyophilize the scaffold-covered plate for 24 hours after freezing.
Plasma coat the dried scaffolds.
If no plasma coater is available, submerge scaffolds in 1% antibiotic-antimycotic (Anti-Anti) in phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Incubate the submerged scaffolds at 37 °C overnight.
Place the plate into the plasma chamber and remove the lid.
Run the plasma coater at 500 mTorr and medium radiofrequency (RF) power for 30 s.
Submerge the plasma-coated scaffolds in 1 mL of PBS and 1% Anti-Anti.
Take 1 x 10^6 cryopreserved HepG2 cells and seed into a T75 cell culture flask.
Add 12 mL of complete media to the T75 cell culture flask.
The complete media consists of Eagle's minimum essential medium (EMEM) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum, 100 U/mL penicillin-streptomycin, 5 mM L-glutamine, and 1% nonessential amino acids.
Wash cells 3 times with PBS.
Incubate cells in 2 mL of trypsin at 37°C for 4 min.
Tap the flask to detach the cells.
Deactivate trypsin by adding 8 mL of complete media.
Transfer cell suspension into a 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge cells at 120 x g for 5 min.
Remove supernatant above the cell pellet with an aspirating pipette.
Replace the supernatant with 5 mL of complete media.
Resuspend cells by pipetting up and down with a 5 mL serological pipette.
Mix 100 µL of cell suspension with 100 µL of trypan blue in a 1.5 mL vial.
Introduce mixture onto a hemocytometer under a glass coverslip.
Count cells under a microscope using the trypan blue exclusion method.
Adjust cell concentration to 2.6 x 10^6 cells/mL by adding or removing complete media.
Remove excess media by centrifuging cells at 220 x g for 5 min if necessary.
Resuspend cells in adjusted volume of complete media as needed.
Aspirate 1% Anti-Anti in PBS from the well plate.
Seed 50 µL of cell suspension (2.6 x 10^6 cells/mL) onto scaffold surface using a 200 µL pipette.
Allow cells to attach under incubation at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 1−3 h.
Add 300 µL of culture media for a 48 well plate or 500 µL for a 24 well plate after attachment.
Incubate scaffold with attached cells at 37°C and 5% CO2.
